question: At the same retrospective review workload, which saved model ranking covers more positive records?
status: Written before running this supplementary analysis; existing data and earlier results have already been examined. Not a preregistration.
supplement: LR-count reference: each fold K equals the number of saved LR positive predictions in that fold. Uses no new test-label-based choice. Asymmetric reference, not an independently fixed capacity.
capacity: For fixed budgets, K=floor(B*N_fold). Each model selects exactly K rows separately within the same outer test fold.
tie_rule: Sort score descending, then ascending SHA256(ASCII string equal-review-v1|20261108|source_row), then source_row ascending. The same source-row priority is reused across models and settings. May split a tied score group to use exact K slots; this is batch Top-K, not a new numeric warning cutoff.
label_role: Test labels only evaluate selected lists, never choose K, model, weights, cutoff tie priority or budget.
outcomes: cutoff ties and attainable TP range across cutoff-tie choices
comparisons: all models; emphasize RF minus LR, with fold-level counts and pooled additive counts
uncertainty: Descriptive saved-cohort comparison. No independent-fold significance test, population CI, or refit uncertainty estimate. Cutoff-tie TP ranges are combinatorial bounds, not confidence intervals.
prohibited: No fitting, retuning, feature changes, frozen-threshold changes, or selection of final policy from these results.
